newsitem.title: USA: Congress likely to approve SPR oil sale for budget.
newsitem.headline: Congress likely to approve SPR oil sale for budget.

text.p: U.S. House and Senate lawmakers are moving toward including a $220 million oil sale from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to trim the deficit in a catch-all budget bill for the 1997 fiscal year, House aides said on Tuesday.

"That is certainly where we are headed at the moment," said a House aide, when asked whether the proposed oil sale would be included in the broad spending bill that lawmakers are negotiating for the new fiscal year which begins Oct 1.
The aide said a final decision on the oil sale would probably be made later this week.
The House earlier this summer rejected the proposed oil sale in a spending bill for interior programs, objecting to using the emergency stockpile as an easy source of revenue.

But the oil sale was included in the Senate's version of the bill before Senate leaders withdrew it from debate and opted instead to negotiate with the House on a broader bill covering several agencies before Congress adjourns.

"We're operating under the general assumption that they're going to include (the oil sale)," an Energy Department official said this week, adding that the department could begin an auction "almost at a moment's notice."
The government last month completed the sale of 13 million barrels of oil worth $227 million to help fund education spending for the 1996 fiscal year.
